prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: one complete transparent PNG creature miniature for a square-grid tabletop RPG, intended for 48/64/96px display.
Primary request: create the DIRE WOLF identity by replacing only the wolf in Image 1. Image 1 is the style/base edit target: preserve its hand-painted sculpted miniature finish, steep downward three-quarter camera, soft upper-left light, and neutral thin dark grey-brown circular disc with a subdued bronze-grey bevel. Image 2 is an ordinary-wolf contrast reference only; do not repeat its pale diagonal walking pose. Image 3 is the native dire-wolf identity reference only.
Subject and silhouette: exactly one complete, very muscular, long-bodied brown DIRE WOLF in a low stalking crouch, viewed from above. The overall body axis is strongly horizontal across the middle of the round disc: large head and long muzzle on the left, broad low shoulders near centre-left, elongated back and powerful tucked hindquarters on the right. The muzzle turns a little toward the lower-left viewer; not a front-facing symmetric pose. Four plausible legs remain discernible, with one heavy forepaw advancing low toward the lower-left and the other foreleg planted beneath the chest. The belly and shoulders sit low; a thick tail curls inward beside the right hindquarters. Keep pointed canine ears, strong canine muzzle and one coherent body. Do not turn it into a bear, lion, hyena, portrait or oversized head.
Value and colour: deep warm umber-brown coat, broad tawny shoulder and back planes, warm bone-grey muzzle and a restrained light chest patch. This must be materially darker and browner than Image 2, yet with readable broad sculpted planes distinct from the grey-brown disc even in grayscale. Distinguish this animal from Image 1 through the low, long horizontal silhouette and asymmetric side-facing posture, not just colour. No silver neck wreath. Fur detail is subordinate to the long muscular mass.
Framing: output a square 1024x1024 image; centre the almost-circular thin disc at approximately 86% of the canvas width. Show the entire creature, all paws, ears and tail inside the disc with a continuous exposed strip of disc around them. Creature spans about 80–86% of the disc diameter. Leave the top-right 23% by 18% of the canvas free of face or other essential species features for runtime badges; do not draw a badge or reserved-area marking.
Lighting/material: muted matte painted resin or carved miniature, soft light from upper-left, broad intentional highlights and small contact shadow only on the disc. Do not add a uniform glowing edge; no theatrical lighting.
Background: true transparent native alpha outside the disc, clean antialiased edges, no scene and no external cast shadow. Preserve generated native alpha.
Avoid: faction rings, coloured rims, rank, crowns, HP bars, shields, selection markers, text, numbers, icons, letters, watermark, collars, armour, weapons, grass, rocks, fog, terrain, painted transparency checkerboard, black/white backdrop, extra creatures. Exactly one wolf and one neutral base; not a contact sheet.
reference_roles: Style/base edit target; retain shared tabletop material, angle, lighting and neutral disc while replacing creature identity and pose.
Ordinary wolf contrast reference; avoid its light grey diagonal walking silhouette.
Native dire wolf identity reference; brown muscular wolf anatomy.
image_processing: Original built-in image_gen output copied byte-for-byte. No image pixel edit, recolouring, matte, or alpha replacement.

observations: A full warm-brown long-bodied wolf in a low horizontal-diagonal crouch; four paws, inward-curled tail and neutral base are visible.
The muzzle is at lower left and broad shoulders are lower and more lateral than the frontal great-wolf reference.
The result still shares some face and tail language with the ordinary wolf, so 64px same-family comparison remains required.
Disc and creature are contained; right-upper badge reserve contains no face.
remaining_limits: Default shader, dense same-family comparison, relation/HP/rank overlays and motion still require parent runtime validation.
Original output is native 1254 square despite the requested 1024; original master remains unchanged.

static_review.method: Parent mechanically exported original masters with the existing C tool. Existing CJS Chromium capture displayed each sprite at its actual native pixel dimensions, device scale 1. Both screenshots inspected with view_image at original resolution. No creature pixels changed.
static_review.observation: 64px low horizontal deep warm body is distinguishable from the light diagonal ordinary wolf and the frontal great wolf; grayscale retains posture plus value differences.
